question: Why do nurses keep their feet wide apart when lifting a patient?

options.A: To reduce pressure on the knees
options.B: To create a stable base of support
options.D: To increase speed during the transfer

explanation: Spreading your feet gives you great balance and keeps you steady, so you don't easily lose your footing while helping a patient. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is twisting your body while lifting a heavy patient a big risk?

options.A: It puts uneven stress on the spinal discs
options.B: It cuts off circulation in the legs
options.C: It immediately lowers the patient's blood pressure
options.D: It causes the nurse to drop the patient's legs

explanation: Twisting while carrying weight puts awkward pressure on your spine, which is a quick way to get a bad back injury. Always pivot with your feet instead! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should check before moving a patient to a chair?

options.A: The color of the patient's room walls
options.B: The brand name of the hospital bed
options.C: The patient's current ability to bear weight
options.D: The exact time the doctor's shift ends

explanation: Always check if the patient can stand or support themselves first! This tells you if you need an extra pair of hands or a mechanical lift. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: Your patient just woke up from surgery and feels dizzy. What should you do about getting them out of bed?

options.A: Use a standard sliding board without help
options.B: Ask the patient to walk alone to test their strength
options.C: Lift the patient quickly to avoid bedsores
options.D: Postpone the transfer and reassess the dizziness

explanation: Dizziness is a warning sign of weakness or low blood pressure. It's always safer to let them rest until they are steady. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: What safety step must you take immediately before moving a patient into a wheelchair?

options.A: Lock the wheels on both the bed and the wheelchair
options.C: Recline the wheelchair back completely flat

explanation: Always lock those wheels! Unlocked furniture loves to roll away, which is a major cause of patient falls in the ward. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why do healthcare workers count out loud before doing a lift together?

options.A: It helps everyone lift together at the exact same moment
options.B: It distracts the patient from feeling any pain
options.C: It signals visitors to leave the room quietly
options.D: It measures the exact seconds the transfer takes

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Counting down ensures everyone pulls or lifts in unison so nobody drops the weight. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the main reason for using a gait belt during a patient transfer?

options.A: To provide a secure handhold for the nurse to support the patient
options.B: To monitor the patient's breathing rate automatically
options.C: To lift the patient completely off the floor without help
options.D: To keep the patient's hospital gown tightly closed

explanation: A gait belt gives you a safe, firm grip around the patient's waist without having to awkwardly grab their clothes or arms. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h4)

question: When helping a patient move from a bed to a chair, which direction should they generally pivot?

options.A: Toward the side with the IV pole
options.D: Toward the wall for extra privacy

explanation: Guiding them toward their stronger side lets them use their own strength and keeps them feeling secure during the turn. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which type of patient needs a full-body mechanical lift?

options.A: An ambulatory patient who walks with a cane
options.B: A patient who only needs a gentle reminder to stand
options.C: A restless patient who tries to jump out of bed
options.D: A completely dependent patient who cannot bear weight

explanation: If a patient has zero weight-bearing ability, a mechanical lift does the heavy lifting safely for both you and the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is a crucial safety check before using any mechanical lift sling?

options.A: Ensuring the patient is wearing non-skid slippers
options.B: Inspecting the straps and clips for fraying or damage
options.C: Measuring the exact distance to the hallway door
options.D: Checking if the battery is fully charged to maximum speed

explanation: Always double-check those straps! Frayed or worn fabric can snap under pressure, which is dangerous for the patient in the sling. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is using standard equipment for bariatric patients unsafe?

options.A: Standard equipment lacks wheels for smooth movement
options.B: Standard equipment may break under excess weight, causing injury
options.C: Standard equipment is usually too warm for the patient
options.D: Standard equipment takes up too much floor space

explanation: Standard devices have weight limits. Exceeding them can cause sudden equipment failure and lead to a nasty fall. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h6)

question: You need to move a heavy patient higher up in bed. How do you prevent skin damage and friction?

options.A: Pull firmly by the patient's wrists to slide them upward
options.B: Ask the patient to push with their heels while you pull
options.C: Use a draw sheet with another staff member to lift rather than drag
options.D: Grab the patient's ankles and pull them toward the headboard

explanation: Dragging causes friction burns and bedsores. Using a draw sheet to slightly lift and slide the patient protects their delicate skin! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is a vital safety action to take right after helping a patient back into bed?

options.A: Remove all pillows from the bed entirely
options.B: Turn off all the lights in the patient's room
options.C: Lock the patient inside the room for privacy
options.D: Place the call bell within the patient's reach

explanation: Always make sure the call bell is right where the patient can easily grab it before you walk away. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why should a nurse document how well a patient tolerated a physical transfer?

options.A: To prove to the hospital kitchen when meals should be served
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of the nursing care
options.C: To track how the patient handled the activity and monitor for fatigue or pain
options.D: To decide which television channels the patient prefers

explanation: Documenting tolerance helps the whole nursing team know if the patient is gaining strength or getting too exhausted during activities. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h7)
